On the left is an AC voltage source, labeled 5 sin(5t) V, with polarity positive at the top and negative at the bottom; the upper branch has a 100 kΩ resistor; on the right is a 1 μF capacitor, and the capacitor voltage V_C is labeled positive at the top and negative at the bottom; the lower branch also has a 100 kΩ resistor. Reasoning: The three elements are in the same series path, so the total resistance of the two resistors is R_total = 100 kΩ + 100 kΩ = 200 kΩ. From the source 5 sin(5t) V, the angular frequency is ω = 5 rad/s, and the sine reference phasor V_s = 5∠0 is used. The capacitor impedance is Z_C = 1/(jωC) = 1/(j·5·1 μF) = -j200 kΩ. By series voltage division, V_C/V_s = Z_C/(R_total + Z_C) = (-j200)/(200 - j200). The magnitude of this ratio is 1/√2, and the phase is -π/4. Therefore the magnitude of V_C is 5/√2 = 2.5√2, lagging the source voltage by π/4, so V_C = 2.5√2 sin(5t - 0.25π) V.
